hook_text: Two eighths plus three eighths. Is it five eighths or five sixteenths? Half the class gets this wrong.
clip_script: Chocolate slab, 8 blocks. Eat 2 blocks: two eighths. Eat 3 more: three eighths. How much altogether? Count the blocks: 5. And the slab? Still 8 blocks. So five eighths, not five sixteenths. Add the tops, keep the bottom, because the bottom is the size of the pieces. Now the juice jug: one quarter, two quarters, one quarter more. 1 plus 2 plus 1 is 4: four quarters, one whole litre. And three quarters plus three quarters? Six quarters: one whole litre and two quarters more. Count the pieces, keep their name, and spot the whole.
visual_style: Whiteboard chocolate slab with blocks coloured in two colours; a measuring jug filling in quarter steps past the one litre line.
mood: Confident and snappy, with a myth busted.
pacing: The common mistake, the blocks that prove it, then the jug filling to a whole and beyond.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write three fraction sums that make one whole.
